title: Cat Purring
blurb: Understand why cats purr and its meaning

items.front: Why do cats purr when they're happy?
items.back: Purring signals contentment, but also healing and stress relief.

items.front: Can cats purr when they're in pain?
items.back: Yes! Purring releases endorphins, their natural painkillers.
Rapid muscle twitches in their larynx vibrate.

items.front: Do big cats like lions purr?
items.back: Only on exhale—domestic cats purr both ways.

items.front: Can a cat's purr heal bones?
items.back: Yes! 25-50 Hz purrs may speed up healing.

items.front: Why do kittens purr as newborns?
items.back: They’re born blind/deaf—purring helps mom find them.

items.text: A cat’s purr vibrates at the same frequency that promotes bone density in humans.
Cats purr during labor to self-soothe and release calming hormones.
Some cats purr so loud they hit 60 decibels—like a vacuum cleaner.

quiz.q: What is the primary reason cats purr when they are happy?
options: To communicate contentment and relaxation
To scare away predators
To regulate their body temperature
quiz.explain: Cats often purr as a sign of contentment and relaxation, similar to a human smile.

quiz.q: Can cats purr when they are in pain or distress?
options: No, purring only occurs when cats are happy
Yes, cats may purr to self-soothe or signal they need help
Only kittens purr in pain, not adult cats
quiz.explain: Cats may purr when in pain or distress as a self-soothing mechanism or to solicit care.

quiz.q: How do cats produce their purring sound?
options: By rapidly moving their vocal cords using their laryngeal muscles
By vibrating their whiskers
By exhaling air through their nose
quiz.explain: Cats purr by rapidly contracting their laryngeal muscles, which causes their vocal cords to separate and snap back together.

quiz.q: Do big cats like lions and tigers purr continuously like domestic cats?
options: Yes, all big cats purr just like house cats
No, only some big cats like cheetahs and cougars can purr continuously
Big cats roar instead of purring
quiz.explain: Only smaller big cats, such as cheetahs and cougars, can purr continuously like domestic cats, while larger ones like lions and tigers cannot.

quiz.q: Is there evidence that a cat’s purr can help heal bones or tissues?
options: No, this is purely a myth with no scientific basis
Yes, the frequency of a cat’s purr can promote bone density and healing
Only in very rare cases with specific breeds
quiz.explain: Studies suggest that the frequency of a cat’s purr (20-140 Hz) may promote bone density and accelerate healing.

quiz.q: Why do newborn kittens purr almost immediately after birth?
options: To communicate with their mother and siblings
To scare off potential threats
To regulate their body temperature
quiz.explain: Newborn kittens purr to communicate with their mother and littermates, often during nursing.

quiz.q: What is true about the frequency of a cat’s purr in relation to human health?
options: It matches the frequency that can promote bone density in humans
It is too low to have any effect on human bones
It is harmful to human hearing over time
quiz.explain: A cat’s purr vibrates at frequencies (20-140 Hz) that have been shown to promote bone density and healing in humans.

quiz.q: Why might a cat purr during labor or stressful situations?
options: To release calming hormones and self-soothe
To attract a mate
To signal aggression
quiz.explain: Cats may purr during labor or stress to release calming hormones and self-soothe.

quiz.q: How loud can some cats purr?
options: Up to 40 decibels, like a quiet library
Up to 60 decibels, like a vacuum cleaner
Up to 80 decibels, like a busy street
quiz.explain: Some cats can purr as loudly as 60 decibels, comparable to the sound of a vacuum cleaner.
